description:
Goal
Make function-head exhaustiveness evaluate coverage inside the function's declared input domain, so total closed-domain reducers are correct by construction.

Signal
00181 defines only main/0 yet emits four type/no-matching-clause warnings. Telemetry/function facts identify the warned reachable functions as Enum.reduce_finish/1, List.reduce/3, List.reduce_cont/3, and List.reduce_step/3. Their clauses cover their @spec/list domains, but source_diagnostics::check_function_clauses calls domain-free is_inexhaustive over all Fz values. is_inexhaustive_with_domains exists only under cfg(test) and only recognizes list coverage.

Strategy
Derive subject domains from authoritative function contracts/specs and feed those domains into shared dispatch coverage analysis. Do not whitelist runtime modules, hide dependency diagnostics, add wildcard clauses to total functions, or suppress this warning by source name.

TDD
First pin 00181 as warning-free and pin a focused tuple-union/list-domain coverage test. Keep a user function genuinely partial within its declared domain warning. Extend telemetry/tests to identify the owning function/source for warnings if needed.

Acceptance
- The four false warnings disappear on interp/run/build for 00181.
- Real partial clauses still warn.
- Coverage uses the same dispatch model as runtime matching.
- Docs state the domain invariant; all tests/clippy pass.

Authoritative implementation placement
fz-1ah.8 landed the shared Types-backed calculator as integration commit 78152613f. Implement this ticket only as a thin consumer:
- Functions without a declared contract retain domain-free head checking during DefineFunction.
- Functions with a declared contract still emit nested case/with/body diagnostics during DefineFunction, but defer only the function-head warning.
- DeriveFunctionContract may wait on EntryDispatch because both independently depend on FunctionDefined; PlanEntryDispatch does not depend on FunctionContract, so this creates no cycle.
- Once FunctionContract and EntryDispatch are available, evaluate every ContractArrow parameter row separately through calculate_dispatch_reachability. The function is exhaustive only when Fail is unreachable for every declared row. Never union parameter columns or Cartesian-expand arrows.
- Guard predicates remain conservative through the shared graph calculator; guarded functions must not be skipped.
- Invalid/unresolved contracts already diagnose their resolution error and must not invent a misleading coverage domain.
- Keep runtime demand lazy: only demanded functions derive contracts and run contract-aware coverage.

Removal
Delete the test-only KnownSubjectDomain, is_inexhaustive_with_domains, and list_domain_is_covered scaffold after moving its list-coverage intent to the Types-backed calculator. Do not add another diagnostics traversal or domain algebra.

Audit-discovered bounded-variable defect
The first thin-consumer commit a6f4d28b is not foldable as-is. Contract-aware coverage extracted Types::arrow_params but ignored ContractArrow.bounds, even though normal contract matching passes those bounds to Types::match_arrow. Repro:  with clauses for :a and :b is total but falsely emits type/no-matching-clause because reachability sees bare t instead of its declared upper-bound domain.

Required correction
Contract input-domain rows must be projected by an authoritative contract/type operation that instantiates each arrow parameter through that arrow's bounds before reachability. Do not hand-roll substitution in diagnostics. Preserve each arrow as a separate correlated row. Add direct contract/type tests for top-level and nested bounded variables, dependent/transitive bounds if the contract language permits them, plus the release diagnostic repro. Unbounded variables remain conservative rather than being fabricated as finite domains.

comments.text: AUDIT FAIL on 7212a7820. Blocking: (1) domain coverage Cartesian-products parameter and nested tuple alternatives; a 16-field bool tuple generates 65,536 rows and takes 6.24s, so replace with symbolic/non-expanding analysis; (2) FunctionContract independently unions argument columns and invents cross-overload inputs, so preserve arrow correlation; (3) list projection discards element domains, causing exact @spec count_a([:a]) with []/[:a|tail] to warn; (4) guarded functions still skip analysis entirely, allowing declared inputs to fall through silently. Existing gates/00181 passed, but local correctness is insufficient. No fold; return to implementation and re-audit.

RE-AUDIT FAIL on cumulative 155617973. Remaining blocker: tuple-union correlation is lost across sequential field projection. project_domain unions each field independently; branch_state narrows only the child subject, not its parent union, so later fields reproject the original union and invent {:a,:y}/{:b,:x}. Exact total @spec classify({:a,:x}|{:b,:y}) with two exact clauses still warns. Fix must preserve parent/child correlated alternatives through projection and narrowing, with a production regression; then fresh re-audit.

STEP-BACK: three audits disproved the projection-domain approach. Branch commits 7212a7820, 155617973, 2a427e959 are preserved as failed prototypes and must not be folded. The first lossy boundary is ContractArrow Ty -> KnownSubjectDomain; the second is independent per-SubjectId projected state. fz-1ah.8 now blocks this ticket and will build one root-Ty/evidence dispatch reachability calculator shared with semantic analysis. After .8 lands, restart .1 from integration HEAD and implement diagnostics as a thin consumer; do not salvage boundary heuristics.

title: Domain-aware exhaustiveness must not warn on total library reducers
